title: Monocular sequence sampling
text: From synchronized multi-view video we sample context frames along one moving camera, each at its own timestamp, and a target frame at a different view and time. Asynchronous view-time sampling is what lets the model disentangle camera parallax from scene motion.

title: Frozen static prior
text: The pretrained static encoder (24 layers) and renderer stay frozen. Context frames become the static latent z_st, which already encodes geometry and viewpoint. On its own it can render any view, but it has no notion of time.

title: Lightweight dynamic encoder
text: Eight transformer layers take the same frames with learnable time tokens. Frame and global attention are followed by cross-attention into the frozen static features (static injection), so the branch explains only what the static prior cannot: true scene motion. It outputs a time-invariant residual latent z_res and a dynamic mask through a DPT mask head.

title: Target-time adaptation and rendering
text: For a target timestamp, adjacent time tokens are interpolated and drive an AdaLN time module with a zero-initialised residual gate. The adapted residual is added to the static latent, and the frozen renderer decodes the dynamic latent at the target view. Training uses only image losses and the mask loss.
